breakdown.note: collective is measured around the canonical reduce (bf16 pack + TCP all-reduce + widen); compute is the remainder, i.e. attention/head/mHC host matmuls plus weight decode. Read volume is the per-step rchar/read_bytes arrays, so a step that still costs seconds with rchar ~0 is compute-bound, not I/O-bound

bytes.note: rchar counts bytes delivered to read() system calls (page-cache hits included); read_bytes counts bytes that came from the block device, so a warm page cache shows rchar > 0 and read_bytes near zero

resident_cache.note: raw stored bytes of every plan slice and every non-Engram checkpoint tensor, read exactly once at startup; Engram tables stay on NVMe and are paged by row range

shard.plan_rule: routed experts column/row; attention, embed, head, shared, router, mHC, norms, engram replicated (Phase 1)
shard.resident_source: in-process cache of every non-Engram tensor

collective.label: tcp-hostonly/world4
collective.canonical_rule: bf16 payloads, f32 ascending-rank sum, one bf16 RNE round; world 1 is a strict no-op

notes: Phase 1 shards only the routed experts; the replicated remainder is numerically a no-op but is not vLLM's TP=4 layout.
One all-reduce per layer (40) plus no gather; the routed output is the only sharded seam.
Tokens are greedy argmax over the replicated head, so every rank must agree without a token gather.
